title: How to Fix Nail Pops in Drywall
metaDescription: Small bumps or rings showing through your wall or ceiling paint? Those are nail pops. Here's how to fix them permanently in about 20 minutes each.
symptom: Small raised bumps or circular cracks in the paint, usually in a line along a wall or ceiling, where the drywall was originally fastened to a stud.
estimatedTime: 20-30 minutes per nail pop, plus drying time

steps.heading: Understand what's happening
steps.body: A nail pop happens when the original nail holding the drywall to a stud works its way slightly out over time (often from lumber shrinking/settling), pushing a small bump through the paint. The fix isn't to hammer it back in — that often just pops again.

steps.heading: Break through the paint over the pop
steps.body: Use a utility knife to score an X or small circle over the raised bump, cutting through the paint layer down to the nail head.

steps.heading: Drive a drywall screw nearby instead
steps.body: About 1-2 inches above or below the popped nail (still on the same stud), drive a drywall screw in until its head dips slightly below the surface without tearing the paper — this re-secures the drywall to the stud properly.

steps.heading: Remove or set the old nail
steps.body: If the original nail is loose, pull it out. If it's still fairly seated, tap it back in slightly and drive it just below the surface — the new screw is doing the real holding work now, not the nail.

steps.heading: Fill both spots with joint compound
steps.body: Apply a thin coat of joint compound over the screw dimple and the old nail spot, feathering the edges. Let dry, then sand smooth.

steps.heading: Apply a second thin coat if needed
steps.body: Compound shrinks slightly as it dries — a quick second coat over any remaining dip gets it fully flush before sanding a final time.

steps.heading: Prime and touch up paint
steps.body: Prime the patched spots before painting so they don't flash (show through) differently than the surrounding wall once painted.

whenToCallAPro: A handful of isolated nail pops are a normal, easy DIY fix. If you're seeing many pops across a large area, sagging in the ceiling, or pops paired with cracking, that can point to a framing or moisture issue worth having a contractor assess.
safetyWarnings: Wear eye protection when driving screws overhead into a ceiling.
Wear a dust mask when sanding dried joint compound.
